probe: MPD TUI live-refresh + DAG rendering, real PTY capture
question: Do the MPD TUI sidebar panel and the MPD full-screen scene actually refresh live (no key press) when the MPD team record changes on disk, and which DAG rendering (rounded boxes / dense list / rail) does each draw?

method.host: dsh-tui 0.14.0 (launcher: /home/haroldzhao/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin/dsh-tui), linked into a SANDBOX copy of the real profile ~/.dsh/profiles/dsh-tui (node_modules copied; the @mpd-dsh/mpd symlink re-pointed at this checkout)
method.isolation: per-run mktemp sandbox: DSH_HOME=<sb>/dshhome, HOME=<sb>/home, workspace=<sb>/ws, XDG/npm caches inside <sb>; the real ~/.dsh was READ ONLY (profile copy + credentials copied in), never written
method.pty: tmux 3.6, private socket, `tmux -f /dev/null -S <sb>/tui.sock new-session -d -x <COLS> -y <ROWS> -c <sb>/ws`, then `send-keys "env -i PATH=… DSH_HOME=… HOME=… TERM=xterm-256color DSH_TUI_LANG=en DSH_TUI_NO_LAUNCHPAD=1 DSH_TUI_WORKSPACE_TARGET=… dsh-tui" Enter`
method.capture: tmux capture-pane -e -p -J (raw ANSI) and tmux capture-pane -p -J (plain), never a re-typed transcript
method.fixtures: docker/ui/team-fixture.mts (the repo's own 6-task board with a failed prerequisite) for the small board; evidence/tui/live-refresh/2026-10-08T07-32-09Z/make-big-board.mjs for the 26-task / 16-rank big board
method.no-keypress: after the surface was opened, ZERO send-keys calls until the last refresh capture; the mutation is a node script rewriting <ws>/.mpd/team/teams/<id>.json in place
method.runner: evidence/tui/live-refresh/2026-10-08T07-32-09Z/run.sh (probe), run-v2.sh (full small-board), run-v3.sh (140x40 + narrow fallback), run-v4.sh (big board)

rows.name: full-2/scene-entrypoint (after the sidebar)
rows.reason: Same focus trap as probe-1: once `/mpd panel` has the input focus, `/mpd team` does not reach the command registry (marker absent for 90s, the frame stays the sidebar frame). The scene arm of full-2 is therefore INVALID as a scene measurement (it measured the sidebar); the scene verdict rests on full-1 and big-2, both of which opened it first from the composer.

rows.name: full-2/narrow-geometry (bonus, 92x40 and 64x32)
rows.reason: At 64x32 the HOST SIDEBAR IS NOT DRAWN AT ALL (no panel border, no MPD page in the pane) — the sidebar has a width floor the host enforces, so a narrow terminal silently has no MPD sidebar. The full-screen scene still opened at 64x32 and still drew ROUNDED BOXES (`task dependency graph`, no `(rail)`) with horizontal panning.
rows.raw: N2-narrow64-sidebar.txt: no `┌MPD` / no `view …` row; N3-narrow64-scene.txt: `│ task dependency graph` + `│ │ ✓ T1   │   │ ✓ T2   │   │ ✓ T3   │`

verdicts.sidebarLiveRefresh: YES — 3 independent runs (full-1 220x50, full-2 140x40, big-2 220x50); first new frame observed at +2.0s after the on-disk write, with no key press; re-open control frames agree with the live frames
verdicts.sceneLiveRefresh: YES — 2 independent runs (full-1 small board, big-2 big board); first new frame at +2.0s; re-open control frames agree
verdicts.sidebarRendering: rounded-box natural layout (`view boxes`, `ranks derived`) for the 6-8 task boards; DENSE LIST (rank-grouped rows + progress bars, no `view …` row) for the 26-28 task board — the frozen LIST_ROWS=24 fallback
verdicts.sceneRendering: rounded-box natural layout (`task dependency graph`, no ` (rail)`) for the 6-8 task boards; RAIL (`task dependency graph (rail)`, `├─▸`/`└─▸` tree) for the 26-task / 16-rank board — the MAX_BOX_RANKS=12 fallback
verdicts.userClaimFalsified: On THIS machine with THIS checkout the reported claim 'the sidebar and full-screen pages lack live refresh' is FALSIFIED for both surfaces; the reported 'DAG drawings are still the old version' is FALSIFIED for ordinary boards (both surfaces draw the new rounded-box natural layout) and EXPLAINED for big boards, where the frozen fallback ladder legitimately degrades the drawing to the dense list (sidebar) / rail (scene) — which is what an old-looking big board will look like.

bounds: The capture proves the PANE the host painted, not which internal tick caused it: the redraw is consistent with the plugin's own intervals (DAG_PANEL_REFRESH_MS=1000, BOARD_REFRESH_MS=2000) but the frame timestamps alone cannot separate a timer tick from a host re-render for another reason.
The mutation is a whole-file rewrite of <workspace>/.mpd/team/teams/<id>.json, i.e. the same path a real `mpdTeams` write takes; it does not exercise the team-record WRITER, only the readers.

Only the MPD DAG page of the sidebar (`/mpd panel`, `/mpd dag`) and the full-screen team scene (`/mpd team`) were measured. `/mpd workmate`, `alt+a` (merged panel), `alt+t`, the Ctrl+A contact and the Web plane were NOT measured here.

One sandbox used a copied 0.14.0 profile with the @mpd-dsh/mpd link re-pointed at this checkout; the TUI host is the real installed 0.14.0, the bundle is this working tree at capture time (no git state was mutated).

Interactive focus: `/mpd panel` takes the input focus and Escape does not return it to the composer on this host; entry-point ORDER (scene first, then panel) was required, and the full-2 scene arm failed for that reason.
The big board is a hand-written fixture (16-rank chain + 10 fan tasks), not a live team; it is realistic in shape, not in provenance.

The working tree was DIRTY and being edited by other lanes during the capture window (src rewrites at 07:37:23-35Z, a dist rebuild at 07:44:25Z); each run therefore certifies the plugin bytes loaded at ITS OWN boot, which cannot be re-hashed afterwards without the module bytes (a `git checkout` was forbidden and would have destroyed the other lanes work).

treeAtCapture.note: The TUI rows resolve packages/<pkg>/dist/index.js (link: install reads this checkout directly), so each run executed the DIST bytes on disk at ITS boot instant. The checkout is DIRTY (other lanes mid-wave) and moved DURING the capture window: packages/mpd-tui-plugin/src/{graph.ts,panel-dag.ts,scenes.ts} were rewritten at 2026-10-08T07:37:23-35Z and packages/mpd-tui-plugin/dist/index.js was REBUILT at 2026-10-08T07:44:25Z — i.e. AFTER big-2 booted (07:43:31Z), so the running process kept the bytes it had loaded (no module hot reload) and every frame inside a run is internally consistent. The verdicts are about the code image loaded at each boot, NOT about a frozen commit: a hash read now is NOT the bytes that were painted.
